record.text: ...Apple is attempting to mitigate initially limited app support for the new device. And vice versa, developers can’t make apps that work only on the iPhone Duo; even if your app is designed primarily for the Duo, it must work on the traditional iPhone models as well. [3/3]

Yes, such apps will look ugly, but they will at least run. The iPhone Duo will likely not sell in tens of millions of units initially, so developers will not have major incentives to support the device from day one – so by “forcing” their apps to run on the iPhone Duo out of the box... [2/3]

I suspect Apple doesn’t want to segment the app development across the Duo and non-Duo iPhones. All iOS apps will work on iPhone Duo even if developers don’t update them to support the new device, and there is no way for iOS developers to opt out of having their apps run on the iPhone Duo. [1/3]

Instead, the existing Apple Pencil (USB-C) will support the iPhone Duo via a software update in 2026, working on both outer and inner displays. The iPhone Duo launches in Japan on October 23, 2026, starting at 364,800 yen, meaning users wanting handwriting input must wait for the future update.
